transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we have a 1,200-unit pilot run of the new fluid-manifold housing requested by a hospital customer, and the sterile-products cell is available next week. Before I make a final decision on whether this proceeds, I need to hear from each of you per our standard pre-run review. Quality assurance, maintenance, and production training — please report any relevant constraints or concerns you have so I can factor them into the release decision. No units ship until we have a documented decision.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed my review of the hospital specification yesterday, and it requires bioburden testing and first-article inspection on exactly 30 housings before the remaining units can enter the release process. However, the customer specification note has not yet been added to the production packet, so we need to make sure that happens before the run proceeds.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: My maintenance check confirmed that the sterilization autoclave can process at most 800 housings per load and requires a 6-hour cycle for this material. I recorded the result in my maintenance notebook, but the equipment-capacity field in the planning system is still unchanged. This means for a 1,200-unit run, we'll need at least two autoclave loads, and the system currently doesn't reflect that constraint.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: My training audit for the quarterly roster found that only 4 operators currently hold the sterile-products qualification required for this pilot. That means the run must be staffed with exactly those 4 qualified operators — no more are currently qualified, and no fewer would be sufficient. I completed the audit, but the updated qualification list has not yet been circulated, so the rest of you wouldn't have seen it yet.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Customer specification note including bioburden testing and first-article inspection requirements must be added to the production packet before the run proceeds.
Must be updated to reflect 800-housing-per-load autoclave capacity and the two-load requirement for 1,200 units.
Updated sterile-products operator qualification list must be circulated to confirm only the 4 qualified operators are assigned to this pilot.
First-article inspection and bioburden testing on exactly 30 housings must be completed and documented before remaining units enter the release process.
Two autoclave loads of 600 housings each (or 800/400 split) must be scheduled, accounting for 6 hours per cycle totaling 12 hours of sterilization time.
Exactly the 4 qualified operators identified in the training audit must be assigned; no additional or substitute operators permitted.
